Implementation plan:
- Files:
  - core/health.py: add a simple health() function returning {"status": "ok"}.
  - tests/test_health.py: unit tests verifying return type and payload contents.
- Design decisions:
  - Keep framework-agnostic: expose pure function health() to be wrapped by any web framework route elsewhere.
  - Return a plain dict to allow frameworks to serialize as JSON consistently.
  - Name function health() and keep module path core.health for easy import.
- Risks:
  - If an existing web framework expects a specific response object, additional adapter code may be needed.
  - Naming/placement might conflict if core/health.py already exists with different interface.

      "content": "def health() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Return simple health status payload.\n\n    Frameworks can import and expose this via an HTTP route.\n    \"\"\"\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n",
      "reason": "Provide simple, framework-agnostic health check functionality."
    },
    {
      "action": "create",
      "path": "tests/test_health.py",
      "content": "import pytest\n\nfrom core.health import health\n\n\ndef test_health_returns_dict():\n    result = health()\n    assert isinstance(result, dict)\n\n\ndef test_health_status_ok():\n    result = health()\n    assert result == {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\ndef test_health_has_only_expected_keys():\n    result = health()\n    assert set(result.keys()) == {\"status\"}\n",
      "reason": "Add unit tests to verify health payload structure and content."
    }
  ]
}
